list.listitem: Paraneoplastic syndromes may be the first sign of malignancy, even before tumor is clinically apparent. C

A "definite" paraneoplastic syndrome may involve a classical neurological syndrome with confirmed antibodies. If malignancy is undiagnosed, it is expected to be diagnosed within five years of the paraneoplastic syndrome. C
Treatment of the underlying malignancy is of great importance in the management of paraneoplastic syndromes. B

The more common paraneoplastic syndromes are outlined below but a variety of rare manifestations also exist, which are challenging to treat given small numbers and lack of clinical trials. Examples include paraneoplastic pemphigus/autoimmune multiorgan syndromes.

Paraneoplastic syndromes are single or constellations of symptoms that occur at sites distant from a malignancy or its metastasis, and are caused indirectly through auto-antibodies, cytokines, hormones or peptides that can affect multiple organ systems.
Approximately half of Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome (LEMS) cases are associated with underlying malignancy, most commonly small cell lung cancer (SCLC) A
In patients with suspected Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS), electromyography is the preferred diagnostic test. C
SOX1 antibodies are specific serological markers for small cell lung carcinoma and if positive, can help differentiate paraneoplastic from non-paraneoplastic LEMS.
Patients with LEMS who are treated with 3,4-diaminopyridine (DAP) or intravenous immune globulin (IVIG) have improvements in strength and fatigue. A
Caused by antibodies to voltage-gated calcium channels (VGCCs) on the presynaptic nerve terminals, preventing acetylcholine release from presynaptic terminals.
Not all cases of LEMS are associated with underlying malignancy.

Suspect LEMS in patients who present with lower limb weakness, diplopia, and distal sensory neuropathy. There can also be autonomic neuropathy, including xerostomia, erectile dysfunction, and xerophthalmia.

On electromyography, look for low resting compound muscle action potential (CMAP), a decremental resonse at low rates of repetitive nerve stimulation (RNS), and an incremental response at high-rate stimulation.
A cutoff of 60% increment improvement cutoff after exercise, EMG has 97% sensitivity and 99% specificity (LR+ = 97; LR− = 0.03) for excluding myasthenia gravis.
A DELTA-P Score can help to predict the likelihood of small cell lung cancer and determine the frequency of surveillance if initial imaging is negative for malignancy.
VGCC antibodies are present in nearly 90% of all patients with LEMS, although their detection is not needed for diagnosis.
Screen patients diagnosed with Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome (LEMS) for SCLC with chest computed tomography (CT) and 18-Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) C

If found, treat the underlying malignancy. Among 16 patients with LEMS associated with small cell lung cancer, those undergoing tumor-specific therapy (chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or resection) showed neurologic improvement.

Amifampridine (3,4 diaminopyridine [3,4-DAP]) is 1st line for the treatment of symptomatic LEMS. 3,4-DAP blocks potassium channels in the nerve terminals, which increases acetylcholine release. Multiple RCTs have demonstrated with moderate to high evidence that it has significant effect on muscle strength score and CMAP amplitude. Pyridostigmine can be added if mild weakness persists with 3,4 DAP alone. The use of Guanidine is limited due to side effects.

3,4-DAPP (3,4-DAP phosphate) is approved for adult LEMS patients and 3,4-DAP for pediatric patients. Recommended dose is 80 mg a day, divided 3 or 4 times a day. Side effects are usually mild, and the most frequently reported are paresthesia

In a prospective randomized crossover trial of 10 patients with LEMS, 8 patients reported they fatigued less easily and felt stronger within 2 weeks of receiving immunoglobulin; only 2 reported improvement after receiving placebo.

After receiving 1 g per kg of IVIG over 2 days, patients with LEMS showed significant improvement in myometry and titers of calcium channel autoantibodies over the following 8 weeks compared with those receiving placebo. Four patients receiving IVIg had headaches and one had meningismus; two patients reported headaches after receiving placebo.
Suspect syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone (SIADH) in patients with euvolemic hyponatremia and symptoms of nausea, malaise, headaches, weakness or disorientation B
Approximately 15% of patients with small cell lung cancer and 1% of patients with nonsmall cell lung cancer become hyponatremic.C
Patients with SIADH associated with cancers have improvements in sodium within a few hours of administration of treatment. C

SIADH is a disorder of water and sodium balance characterized by euvolemic hypotonic hyponatremia due to impaired free-water excretion, which is caused by non-physiologic secretion of arginine vasopressin.
It can also be associated with lung cancer, mesothelioma, head and neck cancers, GI malignancies, cancers of the genitourinary tract, lymphomas, and sarcomas.
Tumor cells secrete antidiuretic hormones that act on vasopressin receptors in renal collecting ducts to reabsorb free water.
If SIADH is suspected from history and physical examination, first test the patient's serum sodium, serum osmolality, and urine osmolality.

To give a diagnosis of SIADH, the patient should be clinically euvolemic, have a plasma sodium level of less than 135 mmol/L, have serum osmolality less than 270-275 mOsm/kg, and have urinary osmolality greater than 100 mOsm/kg. Urine sodium is usually > 30 mEq/L and there must also be normal thyroid, renal, adrenal, hepatic, and pituitary functions and no recent diuretic use.
For more details on diagnostic testing, please see chapter on SIADH.
Treat the underlying hyponatremia based on its acuity and severity of symptoms.

Dietary fluid restriction is recommended by consensus as first line therapy when the condition is chronic and asymptomatic, although hypertonic saline infusion may be needed in the event of acute symptoamtic presentation.

Conivaptan (antagonist to vasopressin receptors V1A and V2) will improve hyponatremia, however, central pontine myelinolysis can occur with rapid correction. Fluid restriction while using conivaptan may increase the rate of sodium correction. A small prospective study of 11 patients showed improvement in serum sodium levels 4 hours after the administration of a V2-receptor antagonist.
Please see chapter on SIADH for further details on treatment.
When you suspect Cushing's syndrome, begin with ordering serum cortisol and plasma ACTH levels and confirm with dexamethasone suppression and corticotropin-releasing hormone stimulation tests. C
The treatment of patients with Cushing's syndrome with ketoconazole, steroid synthesis inhibitors, or surgical removal of the tumor is associated with hormonal responses and symptomatic relief. C
The prognosis among cancer patients with Cushing's syndrome is poorer than among those patients without Cushing's syndrome.B
Cushing's syndrome is associated with small cell lung cancer, neuroendocrine tumors, medullary thyroid cancers, prostate cancer, cervical cancer, and pheochromocytoma.
50% of ectopic Cushing's syndrome is caused by small cell lung cancer.
15% to 20% of Cushing's syndrome is caused by ectopic ACTH production by malignant tumor cells.
In ectopic ACTH syndrome, tumors secrete ACTH or ACTH-like proteins which stimulate adrenal glands to produce cortisol.

Suspect Cushing's syndrome in the patient with facial phlethora, proximal muscle weakness, unexplained osteoporosis in a young age, and reddish purple striae. central obesity, round facies, striae, and a buffalo hump.
Consensus on diagnosis and management of Cushing's disease was recently updated.
Patients with slowly growing ACTH-producing masses, such as carcinoid tumors, have the time to develop classic Cushingoid features.

Approximately two-thirds of patients with small cell lung cancer-induced Cushing's syndrome will present with edema and hyperpigmentation; half with muscle weakness, bruising, hypertension and weight gain; approximately one-third with acne; and one quarter with psychiatric disease. Approximately one-third of patients with small cell lung cancer-induced Cushing's syndrome have diabetes and 70% have hypokalemia. ,.
Please refer to the chapter on Cushing's syndrome for more details on diagnosing Cushing's syndrome.
Two measuresments of a urine free cortisol or late night salivary cortisol, or overnight dexamethasone suppresion test (DST) is recommended as initial testing for Cushing's syndrome.
If the above tests are abnormal, a dexamethasone CRH test is recommended.

A retrospective study found that of 40 patients with ectopic ACTH production and resulting Cushing's syndrome, none had a midnight cortisol level of less than 1.7 µg/dL or suppression to the low-dose dexamethasone suppression test.

Once Cushing's syndrome has been confirmed, further testing will need to be performed to distinguish Cushing's disease from cushing's disease. Peak serum cortisol levels greater than 21 µg/dL and peak plasma ACTH greater than 45 pg/mL is 95% sensitive and 91% specific for ACTH-dependent Cushing's syndrome.

Once you have determined that ectopic production of ACTH exists, start with a chest x-ray and/or CT scan of the neck, chest, and abdomen to search for tumor sources since removing the source of ectopic ACTH production is the preferred treatment.

If chest x-ray and CT do not reveal the source, scintigraphy with octreotide and bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling (IPSS; done before and after corticotropin-releasing hormone stimulation) are reasonable options. But IPSS was negative in 66 of 67 patients; its limitations include operator error, high cost, rare thromboembolic, and neurologic complications.

Octreotide scintigraphy was performed in 43 patients with ectopic ACTH production. In 21 of the patients, the scan correctly identified the ACTH source. Among 13 of these patients, in whom the other studies failed to identify a source, 3 had occult tumors seen on scintigraphy.

Whole body venous catheterization and sampling was found to be less helpful in 1 retrospective study. Among 22 patients in whom the source of ectopic ACTH production was evident after basic imaging and who underwent whole body venous catheterization, the source of ACTH production was found in only 4.
If all imaging remains negative, the consensus is to rescan patients every 6 months to 12 months. There are no mortality data to validate these intervals.
Please see the Cushing's syndrome chapter for more details on diagnosing Cushing's syndrome.

The Endocrine Society recommends that the first-line treatment for endogenous Cushing’s syndrome be the removal of the tumor unless surgery is not possible or unlikely to address the excess cortisol. Surgical resection is considered the definitive treatment for paraneoplastic Cushing's syndrome.
If surgical resection of the primary ACTH-producing tumor is not possible, bilateral adrenalectomy may be of some symptomatic benefit, but no survival benefit has been proved.
In a retrospective review, among 15 patients with ectopic production of ACTH treated with ketoconazole, 10 had hormonal responses but only 4 had symptomatic relief.
Other inhibitors of steroidogenesis have been used, including metyrapone, RU 486, aminoglutethimide, etomidate and para-dichlorodiphenyldichloroethane.
Please see the Cushing's syndrome chapter for more details on treating Cushing's syndrome.
Ectopic ACTH production in patients with small cell lung cancer is associated with shorter survival, poorer response to chemotherapy, and increased risk of infection.

Cushing's syndrome is a negative prognostic factor for patients with small cell lung cancer: 82% of patients with small cell lung cancer and Cushing's died within 2 weeks of treatment initiation compared with 25% of small cell lung cancer patients without Cushing's. Of the patients who died in the first 2 weeks of therapy, patients with small cell lung cancer and Cushing's were more likely to die of fungal or protozoal infections (46%) than were patients with small cell lung cancer alone (8%).
Control of hypercortisolemia is associated with better prognosis, and it has been suggested that control of steroidogenesis prior to initiation of chemotherapy may be beneficial.
Patients with humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy (HHM) have elevated serum parathyroid hormone-related peptide (PTHrP) levels and low-to-undetectable serum parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels. C
An elevated serum PTHrP level in patients with HHM is associated with shorter survival. B

Humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy is the most common metabolic complication of malignancies. However, it's incidence may be declining due to potent chemotherapeutic agents. High mortality associated with the disease has declined as well.
Hypercalemia of malignancy affects 2% - 30% of patients with cancer and is associated with high morbidity and mortality

PTHrP produced by tumor cells cross-reacts with native PTH receptors to promote bone resorption, inhibit renal calcium excretion, and increase renal excretion of phosphorus and cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP).
Suspect HHM in patients who complain of constipation, bone or muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, and/or anorexia. Neurologic disturbances such as confusion, depression and even mania can also occur.

To distinguish humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy from primary hyperparathyroidism, measure serum PTH. Patients with HHM will have low-to-undetectable PTH levels because of inhibition of PTH release from the parathyroid glands by the high serum calcium level. In a study of 52 patients, 77% had undetectable serum PTH levels and the remaining 23% had PTH levels below normal. Serum PTHrP is usually undetectable in the normal population.

PTHrp is present in 50% to 90% of hypercalcemic cancer patients with solid tumors, and in 25% to 60% of hypercalcemic patients with hematologic malignancies. In a study of 20 patients with HHM, 85% of them had elevated PTHrp levels, and their levels were significantly higher than the PTHrp levels in patients with metastatic bone disease.
If PTH and PTHrp levels are both low to undetectable, suspect other causes of hypercalcemia, including skeletal metastases, immobilization, vitamin D intoxication, and sarcoidosis.a483
See the chapter on hypercalcemia for more diagnostic details.
In adults with HCM, intravenous (IV) hydration and IV bisphosphonate (BP) or denosumab (Dmab) is strongly recommended.

In 2 concurrent and double-blind randomized clinical trials (RCTs), zoledronic acid ZA (8-mg dose) was more efficacious than pamidronate (90-mg dose) in resolving hypercalcemia of malignancy (55.6% resolution with ZA vs 33.3% resolution with pamidronate; P = .02), and had a longer duration of response than pamidronate.

In adults with severe HCM (serum calcium level >14 mg/dL), combination therapy with calcitonin and an IV BP or Dmab is suggested. This recommendation is based on a study that showed that serum calcium levels at 24, 48, and 72 hours were similar with bisphosphonate-only treatment and combination bisphosphonate and calcitonin therapy despite higher initial levels in the combination group, suggesting synergy.

Bisphosphonate therapy has been shown to normalize serum calcium levels, PTH levels, and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D levels. Even in the presence of these normal values, however, PTHrp levels may continue to increase in many patients following bisphosphonate therapy.
See the chapter on hypercalcemia for more therapeutic details.

Higher circulating levels of PTHrp predict a poorer response to bisphosphonate therapy. A prospective study of 52 patients showed that patients with PTHrp levels of less than 10 pg/mL showed the best response to pamidronate therapy, while patients with PTHrp levels greater than 50 pg/mL had the poorest response.

In a prospective study of 76 patients with HHM who were followed up for up to 1500 days after the diagnosis of hypercalcemia, two-thirds died. Only 1 of 41 of these patients with elevated serum PTHrp levels responded to chemotherapy compared with 6 of 35 of those without elevated levels.
At the end of the 1500-day follow-up period, 31 of the 50 (62%) who died had elevated levels of PTHrp levels while only 10 of 26 (38%) of survivors had elevated PTHrp.
Recent years have seen considerable advances leading to improved understanding of their pathophysiology and increased recognition of new PNS entities and PNS associated tumours..
A number of paraneoplastic syndromes are associated with thymoma tumour including myasthenia gravis, pure red cell aplasia, lichen planus, Good syndrome and limbic encephalitis
Many types of neoplasia are associated with paraneoplastic syndromes including solid and liquid tumors, and scan be categorized by organ systems.
